THE REQUIREMENT

What is the CT600 Return?

Every active UK Limited Company must pay Corporation Tax on its taxable profits. To do this, you are legally required to file a Company Tax Return (known as form CT600) directly with HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) once a year.

The CT600 contains complex calculations based on your Annual Accounts. It factors in your gross income, subtracts allowable business expenses and capital allowances, and calculates the exact percentage of tax you owe to the UK government. Submitting this accurately is vital for avoiding tax investigations.

Why Use Professionals?

  • **Deduction Maximisation:** We ensure every legal business expense is claimed, lowering your final tax bill.
  • **HMRC Formats:** HMRC rejects standard PDFs. Tax returns must be coded in iXBRL format via recognized agent software.
  • **Penalty Avoidance:** Getting the calculation wrong can lead to severe fines or a full HMRC audit into your accounts.
THE RISK

The Cost of HMRC Non-Compliance

HMRC is strict. Missing filing deadlines or under-declaring tax results in severe punitive actions.

Automatic Late Fines

Failing to file your CT600 by the deadline incurs an immediate £100 fine, which increases over time. After 6 months, HMRC will estimate your tax and add a 10% penalty on top.

Late Payment Interest

If the CT600 is not filed, you cannot accurately pay your tax bill on time. HMRC charges daily compound interest on any late Corporation Tax payments, rapidly increasing your debt.

HMRC Investigations

Submitting inaccurate returns, over-claiming expenses, or failing to file can trigger an in-depth HMRC tax investigation into both the company and your personal finances.

TAX EFFICIENCY

Why Precision Matters

Strategic filing ensures you only pay what you legally owe.

Claiming Expenses

Every software subscription, server hosting fee, and freelancer invoice from Pakistan reduces your UK corporate tax bill. We ensure these are fully and properly declared.

The 9-Month Trap

While you have 12 months to file the form, the actual tax payment is due 9 months and 1 day after your year-end. Filing early prevents surprise bills and late payment interest.

HMRC Defense

Submitting a professionally prepared CT600 drastically reduces the chance of an HMRC audit. Our software flags potential inconsistencies before submission.

FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

The CT600 is an official tax return form filed with HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC). It details your company's income, allowable expenses, and calculates the exact amount of Corporation Tax you owe on your net profits.

The CT600 form must be filed within 12 months after the end of your company's accounting period. However, any Corporation Tax you owe must be paid earlier—usually 9 months and 1 day after your accounting period ends.

Currently, the 'Small Profits Rate' is 19% for companies with taxable profits under £50,000. If your profits exceed this threshold, the rate marginally increases up to 25%. We calculate the exact rate applicable to your net profit.

Yes. Even if your company operated at a loss or had zero income, you are still legally required to file a nil or loss-making CT600 return with HMRC, unless HMRC has officially classified your company as dormant.

HMRC imposes strict late filing penalties starting at £100 for being a day late. This increases by another £100 after 3 months. After 6 months, HMRC will estimate your tax bill and add a 10% penalty on top of that unpaid tax.

Once we file your return, HMRC issues a payment reference number. You can pay your tax bill directly to HMRC via bank transfer using your digital corporate bank account (like Wise, Payoneer, or Airwallex).

You can deduct all costs incurred 'wholly and exclusively' for your business. Common deductions include server costs (AWS, DigitalOcean), software subscriptions, freelancer fees, payment gateway fees, and professional accountancy fees.

Yes, a director's salary is a deductible business expense. However, if you are a non-UK resident living in Pakistan, different tax rules apply regarding UK payroll (PAYE) versus dividend withdrawals. We advise you on the most tax-efficient structure.

No. Annual Accounts are filed to Companies House (and HMRC) to show the company's financial position. The CT600 is specifically the tax calculation form sent exclusively to HMRC based on those accounts. We offer a combined service if needed.

If we already prepared your Annual Accounts, we have everything we need. If not, we will need your finalised statutory accounts, a detailed trial balance, and a breakdown of your business expenses to calculate your tax liability accurately.

No. The entire process is digital. We prepare the return, send you a digital copy for approval, and then securely transmit it to HMRC using our certified agent software.
